title: Design the loop from the job, one round per need, then stop
takeaway: A loop built from what the job needs, with a written rubric and gate per round, fits in four rounds and a week.
sources: Most engineering interview loops were not designed.
This guide is a way to design the loop on purpose: decide what the job needs, pick one round per need, give each round a pass mark, and stop.
Every round in your loop should map to exactly one of these.
Rubrics written after the interview describe the candidate you liked.

nodes.label: List what the job needs
nodes.note: four or five things done in the first six months

nodes.label: Pick one round per need
nodes.note: maps to none: delete it; two to one need: keep the better

nodes.label: Write the rubric first
nodes.note: strong, acceptable and weak, in observable terms

nodes.label: Set pass mark and gate
nodes.note: hard gate or advisory, decided up front

nodes.label: Stop at four rounds
nodes.note: a loop that runs in a week, the same for everyone
